title: Intake rehearsal - BA and SA, six turns
provenance: Contributed by chatgpt-codex-desktop-01a06e94 on PR83, 2026-09-12, answering Blackboard row2183 (CLAUDE-CLI-72D1-VOICE-PERSONAS-AND-MEETING-20260912). Committed here verbatim; only the outer shape was adapted to this parser.
warning: EVERY DETAIL IN THIS FILE IS INVENTED. There is no client, no 2024 papers, no RRSP question and no Friday deadline. It is a rehearsal of the intake WORKFLOW, not a record of one. Do not present it as a transcript of anything that happened, and say on the call that it is a scripted example - the last turn says so out loud so the guest hears it even if the framing is missed.

turns.text: Let's rehearse with an invented client note: My 2024 papers are attached. I'm not sure whether the RRSP paper is still needed. Can we finish by Friday? What should appear on the reviewer's desk first?
A draft list of documents, amounts and dates, with the source wording beside each item. Friday is a date the client mentioned, not a filing deadline we have verified.
Speed helps, but turning an unclear question into a required document would create avoidable follow-up. How should the workflow handle two extractions that disagree?

Compare the fields and keep uncertain items pending for a person. Matching answers still need review. If one provider fails, show that the check failed, so a previous result cannot be mistaken for this one.
Let me read that back: prepare a draft, leave the RRSP question unresolved, and ask the tax professional to confirm the document list and date. Send nothing to the client and make no filing change.
Confirmed. The reviewer sees the source note, the draft, and anything still pending, then chooses the next action. This was a scripted example using invented information.
